html:
The cousin and son-in-law of the prophet Muhammad, and the fourth caliph, who ruled from 656 to 661. Shia Muslims see him as the first Imam, Muhammad's rightful heir; Sunni Muslims honour him as the last of the four rightly guided caliphs.

Ali grew up in Muhammad's household and was among the first to accept Islam, as a boy. He married Muhammad's daughter Fatima, and their sons Hasan and Husayn were the prophet's only grandsons in the male line. When Muhammad died in 632, some believed Ali should lead, but the community chose Abu Bakr, then Umar and Uthman.

Ali became caliph after Uthman was murdered in 656. His reign was swallowed by the First Fitna, the first Muslim civil war. He fought Muhammad's widow Aisha at the Battle of the Camel and Muawiya, governor of Syria, at Siffin. When he agreed to arbitration, a group called the Kharijites broke away, and one of them killed him in the mosque at Kufa in 661. Muawiya then founded the Umayyad line of the caliphate. The killing of Ali's son Husayn at the Battle of Karbala in 680 sealed the split.
